---
title: "Examples: real-data applications"
description: >
  Index of the worked examples of multiCollglm: five reproductions of
  published collinearity diagnostics on real data, and a comparison with the
  VisCollin package, with a summary of the four condition-number definitions
  on every data set.
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Every example below applies the functions of `multiCollglm` to a data set
that was used in the literature to illustrate collinearity in a GLM, and
compares the result with what was published. They follow the same
structure: context, data, diagnostic with `multiCollglm`, comparison with the
literature. The code of each article is run when the website is built, so
all outputs can be reproduced.

## Index

| Example | Data | Family and link | What it shows |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| [Lee cancer remission](reproduction-lee-cancer.html) | `LeeCancer` | Binomial, logit | Reproduces the values of Lesaffre and Marx (1993) for the condition indices of the design matrix (190.78) and of the MacKinnon-Puterman matrix (329.95), and the ML-collinearity diagnostic. |
| [Nitrogen dioxide](reproduction-nitrogen.html) | `Nitrogen` | Gamma, inverse | Why centering the weighted matrix makes it singular for the canonical Gamma link. |
| [Coal-mine fractures](reproduction-mines.html) | `Mine` | Poisson, log | Reproduces the published eigenvalues of the information matrix (condition index 2093.32). |
| [Body fat](reproduction-bodyfat.html) | `bodyfat` (`TH.data`) | Gamma, log | IRLS weights identically 1: WS, MP and X coincide. |
| [Plastic injection](reproduction-plastic.html) | `Plastic` | Poisson, log | Widely cited values that cannot be reproduced; large effect of the weights. |
| [Comparison with VisCollin](comparison-viscollin.html) | the five above | several | `colldiag()` equals `method = "X"`; where the IRLS weights make them differ; factors, weights and plots. |

## All data sets at a glance

The largest condition index (square-root scale) of each model for the four
definitions available through the `method` argument:

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(multiCollglm)

lee <- LeeCancer
lee$x6100 <- lee$x6 * 100

models <- list(
  "Lee cancer (binomial, logit)"  = glm(y ~ x1 + x4 + x6100, binomial(), lee),
  "Nitrogen (Gamma, inverse)"     = glm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4, Gamma("inverse"), Nitrogen),
  "Mine (Poisson, log)"           = glm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4, poisson(), Mine),
  "Plastic (Poisson, log)"        = glm(Y ~ X1 + X2 + X3 + X4, poisson(), Plastic)
)
if (requireNamespace("TH.data", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data("bodyfat", package = "TH.data")
  models[["Body fat (Gamma, log)"]] <- glm(
    DEXfat ~ age + waistcirc + hipcirc + elbowbreadth + kneebreadth +
      anthro3a + anthro3b + anthro3c + anthro4,
    family = Gamma("log"), data = bodyfat)
}

tab <- t(sapply(models, function(m)
  sapply(c(WS = "WS", MP = "MP", X = "X", RAW = "RAW"),
         function(k) condition_number(m, method = k)$condition_index)))
knitr::kable(tab, digits = 2)
```

These are the values of Table 1 of the manuscript on multicollinearity
diagnosis in GLMs (with intercept). `WS` is the default of the package.
`X` ignores the IRLS weights (it is what `VisCollin::colldiag()` computes),
`MP` is the definition of MacKinnon and Puterman, and `RAW` is the
information matrix without any transformation.
